The AM1 alloy is a first-generation monocrystalline superalloy used for high-pressure turbine blades in aeronautical gas turbines.
The oxidation behavior of uncoated AM1 alloy was investigated over the temperature range 750 to 1300°C.
The stepwise multi-temperature thermogravimetric analysis (SMT-TGA) showed the presence of a transient regime in the oxidation of the AM1 alloy.
The transient regime was modeled as the initial formation of a fast-growing mixed oxide, followed by the gradual formation of a protective α-alumina layer.
Isothermal oxidation experiments were performed to confirm the kinetic parameters obtained from the SMT-TGA and study the nature of the transient regime.
At temperatures above 1050°C, the oxide scale on the AM1 alloy was mainly composed of α-alumina, spinel, and rutile.
At temperatures below 1050°C, the oxide scale contained chromia, spinel, rutile, bunsenite, α-alumina, and ilmenite.
The morphology of the alumina layer changed from elongated precipitates at 800°C to a more continuous and convoluted layer at 950°C and 1100°C.
The proposed model aims to predict the oxidation kinetics of the AM1 superalloy over the entire temperature range, including the transient regime.
The model accounts for the transition from the transient to the steady-state parabolic oxidation regime by considering the gradual formation of a protective α-alumina layer.
The SMT-TGA method provides advantages in terms of reduced experimental time and material required compared to performing multiple isothermal oxidation experiments.
The parabolic rate constants obtained from the SMT-TGA experiments were in good agreement with the values from the isothermal oxidation experiments at temperatures above 1000°C.
At temperatures below 950°C, the transient regime appears to last much longer than at higher temperatures.
The presence of hafnium in the AM1 alloy may contribute to the slightly lower parabolic rate constants compared to the literature data for the exclusive growth of α-alumina on β-NiAl.
The lattice parameter of the spinel oxide layer formed on the AM1 alloy decreased with oxidation time at 1100°C, suggesting a change in the spinel composition from NiCr2O4 to NiAl2O4.
